=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/render_validation_templates.py:352 | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The Python regex character class `[A-Za-z0-9_./~%?&=+:-]` treats `-` in `+:-` as a range. ASCII `+` is 0x2B and `:` is 0x3A, so the range includes `,` (0x2C) and literal `-` (0x2D) — characters not intended to be permitted in validated URL paths.
  WHY: An APP_URL containing commas in the path (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:8080/health,evil`) passes manifest validation but is not in the shell regex character class `[-A-Za-z0-9_./~%?\&=+:]` (no comma there). The shell driver would reject it at runtime, but the manifest should reject it earlier at render time. The manifest and driver regex path-character sets should agree on the permitted set.
- scripts/validate_driver.sh:102 | severity=NIT | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The shell regex character class `[-A-Za-z0-9_./~%?\&=+:]` allows literal backslashes. Inside ERE bracket expressions, `\?`, `\&`, and `\=` each contribute `\` as a literal character (since backslash is literal inside `[...]` in ERE, and `?`, `&`, `=` are already literal without escaping).
  WHY: If APP_URL bypasses the manifest renderer entirely (set directly in the host environment, not via env_overrides), a URL path containing backslashes passes the shell validator. While `curl -q ... -- "${URL}"` with `--` prevents option injection, backslash sequences in URL paths are ambiguous and curl may interpret them differently across platforms. The escapes `\?`, `\&`, `\=` are unnecessary in ERE bracket expressions — the characters are already literal — so they can be written as `?`, `&`, `=` with no loss of intended behavior.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

=== FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2 ===
- scripts/validate_driver.sh:102 | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: In POSIX ERE bracket expressions, backslash is a literal character, not an escape. The `\&`, `\?` each add `\` to the character class, so the shell regex unintentionally accepts backslashes in the URL path. The Python manifest validator's regex `[A-Za-z0-9_./~%?&=+:-]` does NOT include backslash, creating an inconsistency: an env-var-set APP_URL with backslashes passes the shell check but would fail the manifest check. The developer wrote `\&` to "escape" `&`, but `&` needs no escaping inside `[...]` in ERE.
  WHY: A URL like `http://127.0.0.1:8080/path\with\slashes` set via environment passes the shell regex and reaches curl, while the same URL set via manifest is rejected. The security impact is limited (curl still connects to 127.0.0.1), but the validators are inconsistent. Fix: remove the unnecessary backslashes: `[-A-Za-z0-9_./~%?&=+:]`.
=== END FINDINGS FROM z-ai_glm-5_2
